newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Alleged British spy is mentally ill, parents say.
newsitem.headline: Alleged British spy is mentally ill, parents say.

text.p: The parents of a Russian diplomat alleged to have spied for Britain appealed on Tuesday to Moscow and London to show compassion for their son.
Revealing details of mental problems they say Platon Obukhov developed 10 years ago, his parents Alexei and Olga called for Russian and British experts to assess Obukhov's sanity.

Alexei Obukhov, a former Soviet deputy foreign minister and a top disarmament negotiator, said Britain's MI6 intelligence had been wrong to recruit the son of a man "who spent his life and health to rid Europe of the threat of nuclear conflict".
"In Russian we call this "black ingratitude'," he said in an appeal published by the liberal Nezavisimaya Gazeta daily.
Platon Obukhov, 28, a second secretary in the foreign ministry's prestige North America Department, who wrote spy novels on the side, is in prison awaiting trial on espionage charges.
He behaved oddly during a television interview from prison in July, wearing mismatched socks and a homemade cloth cap. He said he had acted in "panicky fear".
"I had a very unpleasant feeling, but I could not escape," Obukhov said. "I was doomed, I ran like a clockwork mouse, I ran and ran until it all ended."
A newspaper said Obukhov had been working on a novel called "Playing at Death" when he was arrested.
It was not clear how much classified information he had access to.
Obukhov's parents said they were shocked by publications which compared their son to the "giants of espionage".

"The fuss in newspapers and on television forces us to disclose a family secret and speak about a most serious mental illness suffered by Platon," they said. He was diagnosed in 1986 but was kept in the dark about his illness.
They said they wanted an independent medical assessment of Platon's health, possibly with the help of British experts.

"We appeal to the leaders of the SIS (British Special Intelligence Service) and the FSB (Federal Security Service) to meet at a negotiating table and evaluate, calmly and without noisy exaggeration...the case of Platon Obukhov."
The parents said Platon was caught in a struggle between the British and Russian intelligence services.
"MI6 is trying to prove to taxpayers that is is earning its bread and butter and the FSB shows that it is not to be fooled," the appeal said.
Britain expelled four Russian diplomats in May after Moscow threw out four British Embassy employees Moscow accused of links to a Russian citizen who had access to classified information.
The FSB said in July that Platon Obukhov had been arrested in April.
